title: Canonical Academy · Linux SysAdmin qualification · Knowledge practice

format.note: The real exams are hybrid (multiple choice plus hands-on tasks in a remote Ubuntu environment). This simulator covers the knowledge part; use training mode per domain to prepare one exam at a time.
format.scoring: Canonical weights items by steps, complexity, and importance. 70% here is an indicative target.

questions.q: On Ubuntu, which command shows only the error-level (and more severe) messages from the current boot?
questions.e: journalctl filters by boot (-b) and priority (-p).

questions.q: Where do you configure log rotation for a custom application's log files on Ubuntu?
questions.e: logrotate reads /etc/logrotate.conf, which includes /etc/logrotate.d/.

questions.q: Which crontab line runs a script at 02:30 every Monday?
questions.e: Fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

questions.q: What is the difference between a line in /etc/crontab and a line in a user's crontab edited with crontab -e?
o: /etc/crontab has an extra field with the user name that runs the command
User crontabs have an extra year field
questions.e: System crontabs (and files in /etc/cron.d/) include a user field.

questions.q: Before running fsck on an ext4 filesystem, what should you ensure?
o: The filesystem is unmounted (or mounted read-only)
The system is connected to the internet
questions.e: Checking a mounted read-write filesystem can cause damage.

questions.q: Which tools can create or modify partition tables from the terminal?
questions.e: lsblk lists block devices; fsck checks filesystems.

questions.q: User 'marco' must change password every 90 days. Which command applies this?
questions.e: chage -l marco shows the current aging policy.

questions.q: Where are password complexity rules such as minimum length typically configured on Ubuntu with pam_pwquality?
questions.e: pam_pwquality reads its settings from pwquality.conf.

questions.q: What is the safest way to give the group 'deploy' permission to restart nginx with sudo?
o: Create a file in /etc/sudoers.d/ with visudo -f and a rule limited to that command
Edit /etc/sudoers with nano and add ALL=(ALL) ALL
questions.e: visudo checks syntax before saving; limiting commands follows least privilege.

questions.q: On Ubuntu, which group grants a user full sudo rights by default?
questions.e: RHEL-family systems use wheel; Ubuntu uses sudo.

questions.q: Which commands create an Ed25519 SSH key pair and copy the public key to a server?
questions.e: Only the public key is copied; the private key stays on the client.

questions.q: Which permissions are appropriate for ~/.ssh/authorized_keys?
o: 600 (read and write for the owner only)
questions.e: sshd refuses keys if files are writable by others (StrictModes).

questions.q: A shared directory must ensure that new files inherit the directory's group. Which permission bit should be set?
questions.e: The sticky bit prevents users from deleting others' files.

questions.q: Which command finds files in /var/log modified in the last 24 hours?
questions.e: -mtime -1 means less than one day ago.

questions.q: Which command prints lines in app.log that contain either ERROR or FATAL?
questions.e: -E enables extended regular expressions; -v would invert the match.

questions.q: Which command replaces every 'http://' with 'https://' in config.txt, editing the file in place?
questions.e: Redirecting to the same file you read would truncate it.

questions.q: Which redirection appends both standard output and standard error of a command to out.log?
questions.e: The order matters: redirect stdout first, then duplicate stderr onto it.

questions.q: Which command shows the differences between two configuration files in unified format?
questions.e: Unified diffs are the format used by patch and Git.

questions.q: Which commands manage users and groups on Ubuntu?
o: usermod -aG docker alice (add to a supplementary group)
questions.e: usermod -aG keeps existing groups while adding a new one.

questions.q: A file is owned by root:root and must be owned by user 'app' and group 'www-data'. Which command?
questions.e: chown user:group changes both.

questions.q: Where are most traditional system logs written on Ubuntu, in addition to the journal?
questions.e: RHEL-family systems use /var/log/messages; Ubuntu uses /var/log/syslog via rsyslog.

questions.q: What does the octal mode 750 mean for a directory?
o: Owner rwx, group r-x, others no access
questions.e: 4 = read, 2 = write, 1 = execute.

questions.q: Which file defines system-wide defaults such as PASS_MAX_DAYS for new users?
questions.e: Changes apply to newly created users; use chage for existing ones.

questions.q: Which command shows the last 50 lines of a log and keeps printing new lines?
questions.e: journalctl -f is the equivalent for the journal.

questions.q: A login problem must be investigated. Which log on Ubuntu records authentication events such as sudo and SSH logins?
questions.e: auth.log is written by rsyslog; the same events are in the journal.

questions.q: Where are persistent network configurations defined on modern Ubuntu releases?
questions.e: Netplan generates configuration for systemd-networkd or NetworkManager.

questions.q: You edited a netplan file on a remote machine. Which command applies it but rolls back automatically if you lose connectivity and do not confirm?
questions.e: netplan try waits for confirmation before keeping the change.

questions.q: On Ubuntu Desktop, which renderer does netplan usually delegate to?
questions.e: Desktop uses NetworkManager; Server usually uses systemd-networkd.

questions.q: Which command shows the ARP/neighbour table that maps IP addresses to MAC addresses?
questions.e: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to layer 2 MAC addresses in the local network.

questions.q: Which statements about MAC addresses and layer 2 are correct?
o: A MAC address is 48 bits, usually written as six hexadecimal pairs
The broadcast MAC address ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff reaches all hosts in the same layer 2 domain
Routers forward layer 2 broadcasts to the internet
A MAC address is the same as an IPv4 address
ARP is used to find the IP of a domain name
questions.e: Broadcasts stay in their layer 2 segment; DNS resolves names.

questions.q: How often are Ubuntu LTS releases published, and how long is standard security maintenance?
o: Every two years in April, with 5 years of standard support (extendable with Ubuntu Pro)
Every 6 months, with 9 months of support
Every year, with 3 years of support
Every 4 years, with 10 years of standard support
questions.e: Interim releases come every six months and get 9 months of support.

questions.q: What does the version number 24.04 mean?
questions.e: Ubuntu uses YY.MM versioning; point releases are 24.04.1, 24.04.2, and so on.

questions.q: Which command upgrades an Ubuntu system to the next release?
questions.e: LTS-to-LTS upgrades are normally offered after the first point release.

questions.q: Which bodies are part of Ubuntu community governance?
o: The Linux Foundation board of directors
questions.e: See the Ubuntu governance pages for the roles of each body.

questions.q: Which statement about the GPL and permissive licenses such as MIT is correct?
o: The GPL is copyleft: distributed derivative works must be released under the same license; MIT allows reuse in proprietary software with attribution
MIT is copyleft and GPL is permissive
Open source software cannot be sold
questions.e: The Apache License 2.0 is permissive and includes an explicit patent grant.

questions.q: You changed GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub. What must you run for the change to take effect at next boot?
o: Nothing, it is read at boot
questions.e: update-grub regenerates /boot/grub/grub.cfg.

questions.q: After adding a kernel module that must be available early in boot, which command regenerates the initial RAM filesystem?
questions.e: initramfs contains the drivers and scripts needed to mount the root filesystem.

questions.q: Which tool lists the recommended proprietary drivers (for example GPU or Wi-Fi) for the hardware and can install them?
questions.e: ubuntu-drivers list and ubuntu-drivers install.

questions.q: Which sequence creates an LVM logical volume on a new disk /dev/sdb?
o: pvcreate /dev/sdb, vgcreate data /dev/sdb, lvcreate -n lv1 -L 10G data
questions.e: Physical volume, volume group, logical volume; then create a filesystem on the LV.

questions.q: Which command extends a logical volume by 5 GiB and resizes its filesystem in one step?
questions.e: -r (--resizefs) calls the appropriate filesystem resize tool.

questions.q: Before a risky upgrade, you want a point-in-time copy of an LVM volume. Which command creates an LVM snapshot?
questions.e: The snapshot needs enough space to store changes made after it.

questions.q: Which statements about snaps compared to deb packages are correct?
o: Snaps bundle their dependencies and run with confinement
Snaps update automatically in the background by default
questions.e: snap list, snap refresh, and snap revert manage snaps.

questions.q: Which command shows which version of a package would be installed and from which repository?
questions.e: apt show PACKAGE shows its description and metadata.

questions.q: Which command lists packages that have upgrades available?
questions.e: Run sudo apt update first to refresh the package lists.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'apt upgrade' and 'apt full-upgrade'?
o: full-upgrade can remove installed packages if needed to resolve dependencies
upgrade installs a new Ubuntu release
questions.e: upgrade never removes packages.

questions.q: Which package and configuration files enable automatic security updates?
questions.e: By default Ubuntu installs security updates automatically.

questions.q: How do you add an internal root CA certificate to Ubuntu's system trust store?
o: Copy the .crt file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run sudo update-ca-certificates
questions.e: Applications using the system store will trust it.

questions.q: Which tools are commonly used to join an Ubuntu machine to an Active Directory domain?
questions.e: realmd discovers the domain and configures SSSD.

questions.q: User 'giulia' must have read and write access to /srv/project without changing the owner or group. Which command?
questions.e: getfacl shows ACLs; -d sets default ACLs for new files.

questions.q: In PKI, what does a certificate authority (CA) do?
o: It signs certificates, vouching that a public key belongs to an identity
It encrypts all network traffic itself
questions.e: Private keys must remain with their owners.

questions.q: Which command enables a service to start at boot and starts it immediately?
questions.e: enable creates the symlinks; --now also starts it.

questions.q: You want a backup script to run daily, even if the server was off at the scheduled time. Which systemd timer setting helps?
questions.e: Persistent=true runs missed jobs at the next boot.

questions.q: Which command lists systemd timers and when they will run next?
questions.e: Each .timer activates a matching .service unit.

questions.q: You added a line to /etc/exports for an NFS share. Which command applies the change without restarting the server?
questions.e: The NFS server package on Ubuntu is nfs-kernel-server.

questions.q: Which command adds a Samba password for an existing Linux user?
questions.e: testparm checks smb.conf syntax.

questions.q: Before reloading nginx, how do you check that the configuration is valid?
questions.e: apache2ctl configtest is the Apache equivalent.

questions.q: How do you enable an Apache site defined in /etc/apache2/sites-available/app.conf on Ubuntu?
o: sudo a2ensite app && sudo systemctl reload apache2
questions.e: a2enmod enables modules; a2ensite enables sites.

questions.q: What is Ubuntu autoinstall?
o: A way to automate Ubuntu Server installation with a YAML configuration, often delivered through cloud-init user data
A tool that installs all available packages
A snap that upgrades the kernel
questions.e: Autoinstall answers the installer's questions in advance.

questions.q: Which services are needed to boot the Ubuntu Server installer over the network with PXE (legacy BIOS)?
o: DHCP to provide the boot information
TFTP (or HTTP for UEFI) to serve the boot files
questions.e: The client obtains an address and boot file location from DHCP, then downloads the files.

questions.q: A cloud-init configuration did not apply as expected. Where do you look first?
questions.e: cloud-init status --wait is useful in scripts.

questions.q: What must the first line of a cloud-init user-data file in YAML format be?
questions.e: cloud-init uses the header to recognize the format.

questions.q: You forgot the root password and must boot into a minimal maintenance environment. What can you add to the kernel command line in GRUB?
o: systemd.unit=rescue.target (or emergency.target for an even more minimal shell)
questions.e: rescue.target is the single-user mode in systemd.

questions.q: Which ufw commands allow SSH and then activate the firewall with the default policies?
o: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH, then sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw enable, then sudo ufw allow 22 from another session
sudo iptables -F, then sudo ufw on
questions.e: Allow SSH before enabling to avoid locking yourself out.

questions.q: Which command shows ufw rules with default policies and logging status?
questions.e: ufw is a front end that writes iptables/nftables rules.

questions.q: How do you list the current iptables rules with packet counters and numeric addresses?
questions.e: -F flushes rules; do not use it to list.

questions.q: How do you create a system user for a service, without a home directory or a login shell?
questions.e: System users have UIDs below 1000 and typically a nologin shell.

questions.q: Which settings harden the OpenSSH server?
o: Port 22 opened to everyone with no logs
questions.e: On Ubuntu, drop-in files go in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/.

questions.q: Which command lists running services?
questions.e: --state also accepts values such as failed or inactive.

questions.q: Which command lists unit files that are disabled?
questions.e: list-unit-files shows installed units and their enablement state.

questions.q: A process ignores SIGTERM and must be stopped. Which signal cannot be caught or ignored?
questions.e: Try SIGTERM first so the process can exit cleanly.

questions.q: Which command lowers the priority of the running process with PID 4242?
questions.e: Higher nice values mean lower priority.

questions.q: Which command shows all processes with their user, CPU, and memory usage?
questions.e: top and htop show the same information interactively.

questions.q: Which package provides a PostgreSQL server on Ubuntu, and how is it managed?
o: postgresql, managed with systemctl and the postgres system user
questions.e: Ubuntu documentation describes installing and configuring PostgreSQL.

questions.q: Which command shows the logs of the nginx service since one hour ago?
questions.e: nginx also writes access and error logs under /var/log/nginx/.

questions.q: After editing a systemd unit file, what must you run before restarting the service?
questions.e: daemon-reload makes systemd re-read unit files.

questions.q: Which statements about keeping automation scripts in git are correct?
o: Changes are tracked and can be reviewed and reverted
Secrets should not be committed; use a secrets manager or environment-specific files excluded with .gitignore
Git automatically runs the scripts on servers
Git replaces the need for testing
Every commit must be signed by Canonical
questions.e: Version control is the base of DevOps workflows.

questions.q: What is the role of Ansible in a server automation workflow?
o: Configure many hosts in an idempotent way over SSH, with playbooks written in YAML
questions.e: Ansible is agentless and uses SSH.

questions.q: What is Landscape?
o: Canonical's tool to manage, monitor, and patch many Ubuntu machines centrally
questions.e: Landscape is part of the Ubuntu Pro offering and can also be self-hosted.

questions.q: Which command attaches a machine to an Ubuntu Pro subscription?
questions.e: pro status shows which services are enabled.

questions.q: What does Livepatch provide?
o: Critical kernel security fixes applied without rebooting
Automatic upgrades to the next Ubuntu release
questions.e: A reboot is still needed eventually to load a new kernel.

questions.q: What does Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM) provide?
o: Security updates beyond standard support, for main (esm-infra) and universe (esm-apps) packages
questions.e: ESM is available through Ubuntu Pro.

questions.q: Which command launches an Ubuntu 24.04 system container with LXD?
questions.e: Add --vm to launch a virtual machine instead.

questions.q: What is the difference between an LXD system container and a Docker application container?
o: An LXD system container runs a full Linux userspace with init and multiple services; a Docker container typically runs a single application process
LXD containers include their own kernel
questions.e: Both share the host kernel; LXD can also run VMs.

questions.q: Which command opens a shell inside an LXD instance named web1?
questions.e: lxc list shows instances and their addresses.

questions.q: Which command lists all libvirt virtual machines, including stopped ones?
questions.e: virt-manager is the graphical client.

questions.q: How do you check whether a host supports KVM hardware acceleration on Ubuntu?
questions.e: KVM needs CPU virtualization extensions enabled in firmware.

questions.q: Which Docker command runs an nginx container in the background, mapping host port 8080 to container port 80?
questions.e: The format is HOST:CONTAINER.

questions.q: Which command shows listening TCP and UDP sockets with the owning processes?
questions.e: ss is part of iproute2 and replaces netstat.

questions.q: Which command queries the A record of example.com using the DNS server 1.1.1.1 and prints only the answer?
questions.e: Comparing answers from different resolvers helps isolate DNS problems.

questions.q: Which command captures DNS traffic on interface eth0 without resolving names?
questions.e: -w file.pcap saves the capture for analysis.

questions.q: Which iproute2 commands show addresses and routes?
questions.e: ip -s link shows interface statistics such as errors and drops.

questions.q: A server is slow. The load average is high, but CPU usage is low and vmstat shows a high 'wa' value. What does this suggest?
o: Processes are waiting for I/O, so storage is a likely bottleneck
There is too much free memory
questions.e: iostat (sysstat) shows per-device utilization.

questions.q: An application was killed unexpectedly and memory was low. How do you confirm the OOM killer stopped it?
o: Search kernel messages, for example journalctl -k | grep -i oom
questions.e: free -h shows memory usage now, not past events.

questions.q: Large packets fail between two networks while small pings work. What is a likely cause?
o: An MTU mismatch along the path
questions.e: Test with ping -M do -s SIZE to find the maximum MTU.

questions.q: Which practices help respond to resource contention on a busy server?
o: Identify the top consumers with top, ps, or iotop
Limit services with systemd resource controls such as CPUQuota and MemoryMax
questions.e: systemd uses cgroups to limit resources per unit.

questions.q: What is the benefit of using cloud-init in automated deployments?
o: The same user-data configures users, packages, and files on first boot across clouds, LXD, and VMs
questions.e: cloud-init is the industry-standard first-boot initialization tool.

questions.q: Which command shows whether Livepatch and ESM services are enabled on a machine?
questions.e: pro enable livepatch enables the service.

questions.q: Which statement about deploying a web app and its database with containers is correct?
o: Database data should be stored on a volume so it survives container replacement
Data in a container's writable layer is kept forever
All containers must use host networking
questions.e: Docker volumes and LXD storage volumes persist data.

questions.q: A host cannot reach another subnet. Which command shows which route the kernel would use for a destination?
questions.e: ip route get shows the selected route and source address.
